> I'm not following, can you elaborate?

The intent here is simply: expose more model choices in the Desktop model picker (to match what TUI already exposes).

**Motivation:**
I sometimes need an older/smaller variant (e.g. GPT‑5.1‑mini), and it was being hidden by the family-based dedupe.

**What TUI does:**
- TUI does not dedupe by `family` at all. It basically lists all models for a provider and only filters out deprecated ones:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/b24fd90fe8a3433333646f61be6ca882b55d1155/packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/component/dialog-model.tsx#L121-L126

- There is already a allowlist for openai codex model provider

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/b24fd90fe8a3433333646f61be6ca882b55d1155/packages/opencode/src/plugin/codex.ts#L358-L364

**What Desktop was doing:**
- Desktop had an extra gating by `family` values, so only one model per family showed up by default, which is why those additional variants weren’t visible.

**What this change does:**
- Stop using `family` to collapse/dedupe the default-visible set, so more provider models become selectable in Desktop (while still keeping deprecated hidden; and if we want, we can still keep the existing “recent window” constraint to avoid showing truly old models). @adamdotdevin

## Verified Workaround (Windows 11, OpenCode 1.1.36)

I can confirm this issue and have found a working combination of workarounds that reduces startup time from **4+ minutes to under 30 seconds**.

### Environment
- OpenCode: 1.1.36
- OS: Windows 11
- Plugins: oh-my-opencode, opencode-antigravity-auth, opencode-mystatus

### Root Cause Analysis
From logs at `~/.local/share/opencode/log/`, each plugin triggers:
```
bun add --force --exact --cwd "..." oh-my-opencode@latest
185 packages installed [118.92s]
```
The `--force` flag combined with `@latest` bypasses the existing cache entirely.

### Working Workaround (3 steps)

**1. Set environment variable:**
```powershell
# Windows (permanent, user-level)
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE', 'true', 'User')

# Linux/macOS
export OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE=true  # add to .bashrc/.zshrc
```

**2. Add to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`:**
```json
{
    "autoupdate": false,
    ...
}
```

**3. Pin plugin versions (CRITICAL):**
Instead of:
```json
"plugin": ["oh-my-opencode", "opencode-mystatus"]
```

Use exact versions from `~/.cache/opencode/package.json`:
```json
"plugin": [
    "oh-my-opencode@3.1.2",
    "opencode-antigravity-auth@1.2.9-beta.3",
    "opencode-mystatus@1.2.4"
]
```

### Result
- Before: ~240 seconds (4 minutes)
- After: <30 seconds

### Suggested Fix
The core issue is that `bun add --force` is used even when packages are already installed and locked. A proper fix would:
1. Check if the exact version is already in `bun.lock`
2. If yes, use `bun install` (respects lockfile) instead of `bun add --force`
3. Only use `bun add` when a new plugin is added or version changes

Hope this helps others while waiting for an official fix!
